newsitem.title: UK: Japan stocks set to pick up after sluggish 1997 start.
newsitem.headline: Japan stocks set to pick up after sluggish 1997 start.

text.p: The Japanese equities market looks set to make a cautious start to next year but its fortunes are expected to pick up towards the end of 1997, a Reuters survey suggested on Wednesday.

Ten analysts based in Tokyo and London gave an average prediction of nearly 23,800 points for the Nikkei 225 at the end of 1997, compared with Wednesday's close of 20,568.38. The highest individual forecast was 25,000 and the lowest 20,000.
The analysts said the average forecast rise of 14 percent would be fuelled by government plans to promote deregulation and administrative reforms planned in the first half.
The extent of the proposed deregulation would be the deciding factor for the rest of the year but the balance of expectations was cautiously bullish, they said.

Foreign investor interest may heighten as a result of the deregulation and bodes well for further growth in 1998. But most analysts were reluctant to give a forecast for 1998, given the uncertainties of deregulation.
Following are a selection of views on next year's performance of the Tokyo stock exchange:
MAMORU YAMAZAKI, SENIOR ANALYST AT PARIBAS CAPITAL MARKETS
"The Tokyo stock market is likely to make a better showing in the latter half of 1997 after the adverse effects of a planned increase in the consumption tax in April disappear."
SOICHI OKUDA, SENIOR ECONOMIST, NIPPON CREDIT BANK
"The index can rise as high as 26,000, though it's hard to predict at what level it will settle. I think you can take a bullish stance for next year."

"The Nikkei average could push as high as 25,000 by the end of 1997, helped by gradual strengthening of the economy. Foreign investor interest may heighten as the Japanese stock market is a bit behind other markets as far as growth is concerned."
